Are multiple edges between the same ordered pair of vertices possible, or is the input guaranteed to contain at most one label per (i, j)?
Should paths be allowed to reuse vertices and edges arbitrarily many times, or is there an implicit limit on repetitions?
In the output, should numbers be separated by single spaces with no trailing space at line ends, and should each line end with a newline character?
Are the characters '-' in the input guaranteed to appear only where there is no edge, and never as a legitimate edge label?

inline_prompts: We have a directed graph with N vertices, numbered 1, 2, \ldots, N. Information about the edges is given by N^2 characters C_{1, 1}, C_{1, 2}, \ldots, C_{1, N}, C_{2, 1}, \ldots, C_{N, N}. Here, each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -. If C_{i, j} is a lowercase English letter, then there is exactly one directed edge from vertex i to vertex j labeled C_{i, j}. If C_{i, j} is -, there is no edge from vertex i to vertex j. For each integer pair (i, j) with 1 \leq i, j \leq N, answer the following question: Among all (not necessarily simple) paths from vertex i to vertex j whose concatenation of labels on the edges forms a palindrome, what is the length of the shortest such path? Refer to the problem statement for specifications related to: If i = j, is the empty path (length 0) considered. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N C_{1, 1}C_{1, 2}\ldotsC_{1, N} C_{2, 1}C_{2, 2}\ldotsC_{2, N} \vdots C_{N, 1}C_{N, 2}\ldotsC_{N, N} Output Let A_{i, j} be the answer to the question for the pair (i, j). Print them in the following format: A_{1, 1} A_{1, 2} \ldots A_{1, N} A_{2, 1} A_{2, 2} \ldots A_{2, N} \vdots A_{N, 1} A_{N, 2} \ldots A_{N, N} Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 100 - N is an integer. - Each C_{i, j} is either a lowercase English letter or -.
